actual_corpus.normalization: Decode HTML entities; exclude verse labels, footnote marks/content, navigation, title headings and footer from selectable narrative. Collapse Unicode whitespace to one ASCII space; join consecutive verses with one ASCII space. No Unicode normalization, spelling or punctuation change. Retain exact raw HTML independently.
actual_corpus.git_bytes: Raw downloaded HTML witnesses use path-scoped binary attributes; no CRLF/LF conversion. Canonical JSON hashes are portable across display/storage newlines.

index.ordering: One shelf and one complete book; title-only logical page first, then chapters1–4. Source order within each chapter. One-based caller indices differ from stable IDs and native chapter/verse labels.
index.boundaries: 141 manually reviewed punctuation-based sentence units. Speaker introductions remain attached. Closing quotation marks, including spaced nested closers, remain with the preceding terminal punctuation. A standalone unit need not contain a matching opening/closing quote; bounded neighboring context retains surrounding dialogue. Not a universal tokenizer.
index.paragraphs: Paragraph breaks and verse lines are structural whitespace, not automatic sentence boundaries; headings/footnotes are ineligible. Repeated identical text, if present, keeps distinct IDs/paths; no text deduplication.
index.cross_page: Content logical pages correspond to complete source chapters. All four end at sentence boundaries; no split sentence or cross-chapter unit. Future corpora crossing page boundaries require separately frozen ownership/ineligibility. Context never crosses chapter logical page.
index.abbreviation: Manual review found no abbreviation requiring an internal-full-stop exception in this Ruth subset. No general abbreviation/tokenizer support claimed.
index.empty_page: Title-only logical page1 contains genuine source heading, zero selectable sentences and explicit rejection. This is an editorial digital grouping, not a historical blank printed page.
index.offset_unit: Zero-based half-open Unicode codepoint offsets in normalized chapter stream; UI wrapping and source HTML line endings do not change the index.

segmentation_evidence: All141 sentence-ending verse identities hand-reviewed before production; twelve hand-authored exact source/path fixtures; all85 verses independently extracted using a separate regex/entity parser. No runtime tokenizer or expected values derived from production selection.
meaningful_boundaries: Ruth1:12–13 question spans verse boundary and remains one sentence unit.
Ruth4:18–22 genealogy spans five verses and remains one selectable sentence unit.
Multiple sentences within a verse keep distinct stable IDs and exact text.
Spaced nested quotation closers at2:21 and3:17 attach to preceding sentence; following source verse is not polluted.
Source4:17 places period outside the quotation; exact punctuation is retained.
A sentence isolated from multi-sentence speech may lack its opening/closing quote; surrounding context remains source text. No punctuation inserted to rebalance quotes.
Source heading alone forms ineligible editorial logical page1, not a historical printed/blank page. All chapter logical pages end on full sentence boundaries.

source.author: Raquel Martín Hernández

witnesses.fact: Three witnesses: P.Lond.121 (=PGM VII),P.Oxy.56.3831,P.Bon.3 (=Suppl.Mag.II.77). Source dates P.Bon. to2nd–3rd centuries,P.Oxy. to3rd–4th and PGM VII near late4th; note25 records differing scholarly dates. Not three interchangeable complete editions.

P.Oxy. text stops after source keyαγς(1,3,6); numbers continue throughαεα(1,5,1) without corresponding verses. Those are three die-face digits, not decimal ordinal136 or151. Missing verse text is not an adverse answer.

PGM VII nearly complete; other copies help damaged beginning. Author argues common verse order in overlap and no evidence for alternate full versions; this is not authority to invent missing entries or ignore later corrections. Article does not provide all216 mappings.

source.order: Three sequential six-face throws, preserving order
source.ordinal: 36*(a-1)+6*(b-1)+c, editorial one-based storage ordinal, not an ancient decimal numeral
